video.title: Fantasy Basketball Points League Sleepers - All The Yahoo & ESPN Values

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through points league sleepers, meaning players whose Yahoo and ESPN default ranks and ADPs look too low. He first explains a Yahoo injury rule change. IL+ is gone, and the regular IL now takes players tagged out or injured, but not questionable, doubtful or probable players. On Yahoo he likes Giannis, Sabonis, Anthony Davis, Banchero, Ingram, Dejounte Murray, Buzelis, Siakam, Garland, Castle, Randle, Morant, Coby White, Nurkic and McCollum at their prices. On ESPN he likes Wembanyama, Flagg, Jalen Johnson, Reaves, Haliburton, Kyrie, Buzelis, Holmgren, Trey Murphy, Markkanen, Keyonte George, Kessler, Jaren Jackson Jr., Rollins, Paul George, Edey, Ausar Thompson, Quickley and Cedric Coward. He also says Yahoo ranks mix category and points valuations, and that ESPN ADPs update every day from real drafts. In a mailbag answer he now suggests ending head-to-head fantasy seasons on March 28 instead of March 21.

rules.text: Yahoo removed IL+. Players tagged out or injured can now go on IL right away. Questionable, doubtful and probable players cannot.
rules.quote: I plus no longer exists the rules for IIL are different out tags now qualify

rules.text: The old trick of stashing questionable players on IL gave only a small edge. Streaming through the open spot gave more flexibility.
rules.quote: I think just in general streaming through the spot gave you more flexibility

rules.text: He is not sure injury prone players should drop further because of the IL change. They can now go on IL as soon as they are ruled out, without waiting.
rules.quote: now as soon as he misses a game, as soon as he's ruled out, you

rules.text: How much the IL change matters depends on how fast Yahoo updates player statuses to out.
rules.quote: how quickly Yahoo making those updates to player statuses. That will be the big tell

rules.text: Yahoo ranks and ADPs are the same for every format. They do not change based on your league settings.
rules.quote: Remember, Yahoo's rankings and ADPs are format agnostic. There's no, it doesn't matter what format it is

rules.text: Know both your league settings and the site's settings. Yahoo ranks some players for category leagues and others for points leagues.
rules.quote: Cuz some of them they're ranking for category leagues, some of them they're ranking for points leagues

rules.text: Players with a big gap between their points and category value can be mispriced. Target them when the site ranks or drafts them for the other format.
rules.quote: Paulo has a discrepancy in value between points and category leagues and the Yahoo ranks

rules.text: ESPN ADPs will not be fixed later. They update every day from real draft data, so you will see the current ADPs in your draft room.
rules.quote: They update them every day based on the data they receive from drafts

rules.text: When some drafters believe a player might lose his starting job or share minutes, his price drops. That creates value if you think he starts.
rules.quote: But the fact that that exists in multiple places that means that white's value is suppressed

rules.text: ESPN points scoring gives 4 points per steal, so steals-heavy players are worth more there.
rules.quote: Remember, steals are worth four a game over there

rules.text: Drafters are too scared of players coming back from injuries that cost them last season. You can be more confident than their ADPs suggest.
rules.quote: so people are rightfully scared. You shouldn't be that scared, though. You don't need to be that scared

rules.text: He now suggests ending head-to-head fantasy playoffs on March 28 instead of March 21. He thinks the new lottery rules will make late March games more competitive.
rules.quote: I feel like the changes to lottery rules will make those March games more competitive

rules.text: In roto leagues, play to the end of the NBA season with a games cap.
rules.quote: Roto, just go to the end of the season. Put a games cap on

rules.text: A per game rank earned in limited minutes suggests upside if the player's minutes or role grow.
rules.quote: having him at four when he only played 29 minutes a game suggests to me
